Content baseline for the library — complete: all 66 skills, all 234 cases. Recorded in-session via evals/workflow-runner.mjs (Workflow tool, subscription) at k=1, option A (the GREEN generator may read files inside the skill's own directory; RED stays tool-less). 'model' is the resolved id the agents ran on; the runner's 'opus' pin is a harness shorthand and was substituted here. All runs executed on the 1M-context variant of claude-opus-5, recorded under the base id so they stay comparable with API-side runs — run.py compares the model string exactly, so a variant suffix would make these rows skip as 'not comparable' instead of gating.

RECORDED IN FOUR RUNS, staged by reference mass (references+templates bytes over SKILL.md bytes). 2026-08-15, branch main / parent 45aa919, run wf_225687a2-7f5: a 6-skill validation probe, 23 cases. 2026-08-18, branch feat/reference-aware-evals / parent 69cf2d3: the 25 skills with ratio ≥ 1.0, 86 cases. 2026-08-19, parent 35dc048: the 22 skills with 0 < ratio < 1.0, 86 cases. 2026-08-19, parent cb7c83e: the 13 skills with no references at all, 39 cases. Together 66 skills / 234 cases / 1315 assertions.

Refresh by re-running the in-session runner, or `python evals/run.py --all --update-baseline` (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY plus EVAL_GEN_MODEL/EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL). The gate (run.py / skill-evals.yml) fails if an assertion green here later goes red on a same-model row; rows recorded on a different model are reported 'not comparable' and skipped rather than flagged. k=1 is noisy on some cases — accepted; majority voting in the Workflow arm is a tracked follow-up.

Rows knowingly recorded red must not be 'fixed' by editing this file — a recorded false can never fire the regression check, so keeping it is safe, and each one is an authoring lead. 22 assertions scored RED true / GREEN false, i.e. the skill made the model stop doing something it did without the skill: accessibility-design eval:3[7], api-design eval:1[4], api-design eval:1[5], brainstorming eval:1[1], brainstorming eval:1[3], compliance-privacy eval:2[2], dependency-impact-analysis eval:3[1], incident-response eval:1[1], ml-experiment-tracking eval:2[2], mobile-release eval:1[5], performance-optimization eval:2[0], refactoring eval:1[1], release-management eval:2[4], release-management eval:3[3], strategic-review eval:1[0], strategic-review eval:1[4], strategic-review eval:2[4], test-data-strategy eval:1[7], test-data-strategy eval:3[6], test-suite-design eval:1[3], test-suite-design eval:3[7], ui-ux-design eval:3[3]. 7 of those cases score GREEN below RED overall (api-design eval:1 7→6, brainstorming eval:1 3→2, compliance-privacy eval:2 5→4, incident-response eval:1 6→5, release-management eval:3 4→3, strategic-review eval:1 2→1, ui-ux-design eval:3 5→4) and are worth a higher-k re-run before being treated as settled floors. brainstorming eval:1 is the cleanest of them: it carries no references, so its GREEN arm gained only tool access, and it is the one skill in that band with no net gain.
